  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  JULY 27, 2026

A special joint meeting of the Santa Monica City Council and Rent Control Board was called to order by
Mayor Torosis at 4:02 p.m., on Tuesday, July 27, 2026, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa
Monica, CA.

Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Caroline Torosis
  Councilmember Lana Negrete (Arrived 4:07 p.m.)
  Councilmember Dan Hall
  Councilmember Ellis Raskin
  Councilmember Barry Snell
  Councilmember Natalya Zernitskaya

  Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Jesse Zwick

  Rent Control Board Chair Daniel Ivanov (Joined remotely)
  Rent Control Board Vice-Chair Kay Ambriz
  Rent Control Board Commissioner Ericka Lesley
  Rent Control Board Commissioner Kurt Gonska
  Rent Control Board Commissioner Phillis Dudick

  Also Present:  City Manager Oliver Chi
  City Attorney Heidi von Tongeln
  Assistant City Clerk Maria Dacanay-Wisner
  Rent Control Administrator Jonathan Holub
  Rent Control General Counsel Kevin Mitchell

 CONVENE/PLEDGE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened to a joint meeting with
  the Rent Control Board at 4:02 p.m., with Mayor Pro Tem Zwick absent.
  Councilmember Snell led the assemblage in the Pledge of Allegiance.

 STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
 ACCOUNTABILITY  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Councilmember Raskin.
 (LAND
 ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)

 BROWN ACT AND  Rent Control Board Chair Ivanov disclosed that he is joining remotely
 LEVINE ACT  under the Brown Act’s Just Cause provision due to a family emergency; is
 DISCLOSURES  participating with audio and video; and there are several adults present in
  the airport terminal he is joining from but they are unrelated public

  1  July 27, 2026
   members. Due to Chair Ivanov joining remotely, Mayor Torosis facilitated
  the meeting for the Commissioners in the Chambers.

  No Councilmembers or Rent Control Board Commissioners made
  disclosures regarding the Levine Act (Govt Code Section 84308).

PUBLIC INPUT ON  Members of the public Mathew L. Millen and Michael Millman commented
REMAINING AGENDA  on item 11.A.
ITEMS:

STAFF  11.A. Update on Resolutions Placing Proposed Ballot Measures
ADMINISTRATIVE  Amending Articles XVIII, Rent Control Law, and XXIII, Housing
ITEMS:  Policies, of the City Charter on the November 3, 2026 Ballot Previously
CHARTER AMENDMENT  Adopted on July 14, 2026 and Possible Further Direction to Staff to
BALLOT MEASURE  Return with Revisions, was presented by City and Rent Control staff.
UPDATE
  Clarifying questions asked by the Rent Control Board and answered of staff
  included but was not limited to: how the City compares to other jurisdictions
  if the Board restores the hardship nexus, death and incapacity triggers, and
  narrow the definition of “covered occupants”; if other jurisdictions with
  similar or narrower provisions such as West Hollywood, San Francisco,
  Pasadena, East Palo Alto, and Oakland have been challenged; if the concerns
  with circumventing Costa Hawkins and property owners being unable to
  recover possessions were raised recently; what degree do the four available
  options address legal concerns: if the protections in place for limited
  classifications would be in jeopardy if they were pulled out to new
  classifications; if legal precedent exists that could support the City by
  modifying and narrowing the proposed amendments; alternative provisions
  such as adding a tenant to the lease within 30 days of the original lessee
  vacating a unit; protections for remaining the spouses and children; and how
  many people will be covered by this measure.

  Questions asked by the City Council and answered of staff included but was
  not limited to: the likelihood of litigation if the City moves forward with the
  measure as is; if the issue is separate from small rent debt; and if spouses and
  children are protected when the original lessee vacates for reasons other than
  incapacitation or death.

  Considerable discussion by the Rent Control Board ensued on topics
  including, but not limited to: protecting expanded family members; moving
  forward with the measure and Option 2 to modify and narrow the proposals
  on death and incapacitation; Option 4 to not move forward with the measure
  to further explore the issue and other opinions and submit a measure for a
  later election; and taking alternative and conservative approaches by using
  existing housing protections laws.

  2  July 27, 2026
 Motion by Vice-Chair Ambriz, seconded by Chair Ivanov to keep the ballot
measure and add back the death or incapacitation language in Section 1806
on Eviction.

Substitute motion by Commissioner Gonska, seconded by Commissioner
Lesley, to seek Council’s comments before the Rent Control Board votes on
a motion. The substitute motion was approved by the following roll call vote:

AYES:  Commissioner Gonska, Lesley, Vice-Chair Ambriz
NOES:  Commissioner Dudick, Chair Ivanov
ABSENT: None

Council requested a redline version of Section 1806. The City Council
commented on topics including, but not limited to: unintended consequences
in preventing tenants from being unhoused or impacting small property
owners with making less units available to the housing market and businesses
being created with subleases; Option 4 to defer advancing the measure for
more study and community input; the lack of a staff report and making
redline changes at the dais; Option 3 with a new resolution proposing only
to extend just cause protections to single unit dwellings and updating owner-
move in regulations, and deferring limiting evictions based on new occupants
and remaining household members for further study and to the next election;
aligning rent control with non-rent control laws and re-structure proposals to
protect tenants and the City; and the process to develop the amendments with
broad community input and support and its potential to solve current tenant
issues.

New motion by Commissioner Gonska, seconded by Chair Ivanov, to pull
back from the Rent Control Board’s recommendation the limiting evictions
based on new occupants and remaining household members. The motion was
approved by the following roll call vote:

AYES:  Commissioners Dudick, Gonska, Lesley, Vice-Chair Ambriz,
  Chair Ivanov
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

Motion by Councilmember Hall, seconded by Mayor Torosis, to provide
direction to rescind Resolution 11785 (CCS) and return with a new resolution
containing only the items to extend just cause protections to single unit
dwellings and updating owner move in regulations to bring Article XXIII in
line with Article XVIII. The motion was approved by the following roll call
vote:

AYES:  Councilmembers Negrete, Hall, Snell, Zernitskaya,
  Mayor Torosis

  3  July 27, 2026
   NOES:  Councilmember Raskin
  ABSENT: Mayor Pro Tem Zwick

  Councilmember Raskin stated that he voted “no” because: the matter was
  vetted with a great deal of community input and work; community members
  need further protection; and he is concerned about what will occur in the next
  two years.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special joint meeting adjourned at 5:30 p.m., with
  Mayor Pro Tem Zwick absent.

  ATTEST:  APPROVED:

  Maria Dacanay-Wisner  Caroline Torosis
  Assistant City Clerk  Mayor

  4  July 27, 2026
